# EdgeRouterPolicy

EdgeRouterPolicy is a Ziti edge router policy: it says which identities may connect to the network through which edge routers.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | edge router policy, `/edge/management/v1/edge-router-policies` |
| Updated with | `PATCH`: a setting that is left out of the spec is left alone in Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/edgerouterpolicy/edgerouterpolicy.yaml`](../../examples/edgerouterpolicy/edgerouterpolicy.yaml):

```yaml
# Which identities may use which edge routers.
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: EdgeRouterPolicy
metadata:
  name: web-clients-public-routers
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: web-clients-public-routers
    semantic: AnyOf
    edgeRouterRoles:
      - "#public"
    identityRoles:
      - "#web-clients"
      - "#web-servers"
```

More manifests of the kind: [`examples/scenarios/edge-router.yaml`](../../examples/scenarios/edge-router.yaml).

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the policy. |
| `edgeRouterRoles` | list of strings |  | `edgeRouterRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | EdgeRouterRoles is a list of edge router role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of an edge router. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `identityRoles` | list of strings |  | `identityRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | IdentityRoles is a list of identity role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of an identity. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `semantic` | string | `AllOf` | `semantic` | Semantic says how the "#attribute" selectors of one list combine: AnyOf selects what has any of the attributes, AllOf what has all of them. One of `AnyOf`, `AllOf`. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

| Field | Type | What it shows |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `name` | string | As Ziti reports it. |

| `edgeRouterRoles` | list of strings | As Ziti reports it. |

| `identityRoles` | list of strings | As Ziti reports it. |

| `tags` | map of strings | As Ziti reports it. |
| `updatedAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |

## How it behaves

- Roles are `#attribute`, `#all` or `@name`; names are looked up and sent as `@id`, as in a [`ServicePolicy`](servicepolicy.md).
- An identity needs at least one edge router it may use, or it cannot connect to the network at all.
- Roles are compared as sets: their order and duplicates do not matter.

## When something goes wrong

- `no entity named "..." in ...` in `Synced`: an `@name` role matches no edge router or identity yet.
- An identity is enrolled but offline: no edge router policy gives it a router that is online.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
